content_metadata.description: An animated explainer video about the concept of a genome and its implications.

activities.description: Explanation of a gene as a DNA segment containing instructions for producing biological molecules, primarily proteins. Visualization of human genes (20,000) and their function in protein creation.

mood.description: Informative. The visuals and narration clearly explain the function of genes and their connection to proteins.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene explains what genes are and their primary function.

scenes.thematicElements: The relationship between genes and proteins, and their significance in the human body.
scenes.title: Genes and Proteins

videoEditingDetails.description: Similar to Scene 1 with simple animations and text overlays.

activities.description: Demonstration of genes determining physical characteristics (eye color) and influencing disease risk (diabetes).

mood.description: Informative. The scene continues the informative tone with a focus on the different impacts genes can have.

narrativeProgression.description: This scene expands on the role of genes, highlighting their influence on both physical traits and disease susceptibility.

scenes.thematicElements: The multifaceted impact of genes on human traits and health.
scenes.title: Gene Influence

videoEditingDetails.description: Consistent with previous scenes, utilizing simple animations and text overlays.

activities.description: Explanation that genes only account for 2% of genetic information; the remaining 98% is composed of DNA bases. Visualization of this proportion and the potential impact of changes to this DNA on health.

mood.description: Intriguing. The revelation that genes are only a small part of our genetic information and the unknowns surrounding non-coding DNA create a sense of intrigue.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene shifts focus to the larger picture of the genome and acknowledges the complexity and remaining unknowns.

props.name: bar graphs illustrating the proportion of genes (2%) and non-coding DNA (98%)

scenes.thematicElements: The vastness of genetic information and the limited understanding of non-coding DNA.
scenes.title: Beyond Genes

videoEditingDetails.description: Same visual style as previous scenes.

activities.description: Introduction of chromosomes as storage for DNA, explanation of human chromosome pairs (23), and their inheritance from parents. Visualization of a cell, its nucleus, and mitochondria containing small amounts of DNA. Definition of a genome as all DNA within a cell. Emphasis on the near-identical nature of human genomes (99.8%) and the significance of the 0.2% variation for healthcare.

mood.description: Informative. The scene delivers a lot of information in a clear and concise manner.

narrativeProgression.description: This scene links the concepts of genes, DNA, chromosomes, and genome, providing a complete picture of genetic information organization within a cell.

props.name: cell diagram with labeled nucleus and mitochondria

scenes.thematicElements: The storage and organization of genetic information within cells, inheritance of chromosomes from parents, and the remarkable similarity among human genomes.
scenes.title: Chromosomes and Genome

videoEditingDetails.description: Continued use of simple animations and text overlays.

activities.description: Highlight of the 0.2% genome variation and its importance for prediction, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of disease.

mood.description: Hopeful. The scene emphasizes the potential of genomics in improving healthcare, creating a sense of hope for the future.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene concludes by connecting the information presented about genomes to their application in healthcare.

scenes.thematicElements: The potential of genomic understanding to transform healthcare.
scenes.title: Healthcare Implications

videoEditingDetails.description: Same visual style with simple animations and text overlays.

climax.description: The climax of the video is Scene 5 (0:56 - 1:26) where the definition of the genome is presented and its components (chromosomes, DNA) are linked together.

storylines.description: There is a single storyline focusing on explaining the concept of a genome. The storyline builds upon each scene, starting with the definition of genes and progressing to the complete picture of the genome and its healthcare implications.

trimmingSuggestions.description: Scene 6 could be trimmed or combined with Scene 5 as it essentially reiterates the importance of the 0.2% variation.

text_to_speech: Most of us have heard of genes, but what are they, exactly? A gene is a segment of DNA that contains the instructions for the production of biological molecules, usually proteins. Humans have around 20,000 genes, all containing the information needed to build one or more proteins. Some genes determine physical characteristics, such as the colour of our eyes; others can influence our risk of developing certain conditions, such as diabetes, but genes only account for around 2% of all our genetic information - which is made up of more than 3 billion letters of DNA, called bases. While we don't yet understand the exact function of all the other 98%, we do know that changes to this DNA can also impact on our health. So where is all this DNA stored? Almost all of our DNA is arranged into tightly coiled structures called chromosomes. Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, with one of each pair inherited from our father, and the other from our mother. Chromosomes are located in the nucleus of a cell. A very small amount of DNA is also found in the mitochondria - a structure which provides energy for the cell. All the DNA contained in one cell is called the genome. We have one copy of our genome in nearly every cell in our body. Our genomes are approximately 99.8% identical to that of every other human being; it's the 0.2% variation in our genome that interests us in healthcare, as understanding it can help in the prediction, prevention, diagnosis and treatment of disease.

youtube_description:
What is a genome? Find out in this short animation developed by Health Education England's Genomics Education Programme (GEP).

The GEP is developing a range of education to inform health professionals about the impact of genomics on clinical practice. This video is the one of the many educational resources from the programme.

For more information visit https://www.genomicseducation.hee.nhs.uk
